topic: A scientific explanation of the DESI DR1 stellar radial-velocity audit
questions: What does DESI measure and which part of DESI does this repository use?
How does a spectrum become a single-epoch stellar radial velocity?
Why do repeat observations reveal calibration residuals?
What do the baseline audit and experiments E1, E2, and E3 establish?
How are dark matter and dark energy related to this data but outside this audit's direct claims?
inclusion: Official DESI data and instrument documentation
Primary DESI collaboration or Milky Way Survey papers
Stable DOI, arXiv, or Zenodo records
A scholarly review for broad dark-matter inference context
Committed repository reports, claims, manifests, and compact artifacts
exclusion: Press coverage as evidence for scientific claims
Speculative physical explanations for audit residuals
Uncommitted local outputs as required evidence
quality_gates: Every required claim has a source or committed evidence path
Every claim states at least one limitation
Every required concept is covered by at least one chapter
Every notebook executes without error and records current input hashes
The dark-matter and dark-energy direct-measurement boundaries are explicit
